STATUS: NOT COMPILED BY ME. The cluster lock was held for the whole build session:
  spark-one:~/dsv41-opt-20261021/CLUSTER_LOCK  token=claude-w1b-20261108T124446Z (start 12:44:47Z, eta 16:44:47Z)

Brief rule 4: never compile while a measurement window runs, so no nvcc / Triton compile was started on spark-eight.
No compile is needed for correctness: with the binaries absent, DeepGEMM JIT-compiles the new instance at first use
(boot warm-up/capture for the M32 one), exactly as the drafter's current N768 instance was built. `install.py prejit`
builds them ahead of time on each node during the window.

default cache (~/.cache/vllm/deep_gemm/cache): all 9 sm120_m_grouped_fp8_fp4 entries reproduced (True x9).
Analogy check of the "only N changes" assumption: the same one-line 768 -> 576 edit applied to the TARGET's 128-row
N768 entry (0e915d63..., groups 384) gives ec8c0dc58892ba10744e5e0b1c8afe7e, which IS the live target compact
128-row entry that DeepGEMM itself JIT-compiled. So for the target, DeepGEMM's heuristic picked the same tile config
for N 576 as for N 768; the drafter keys above assume the same holds for kNumGroups 128. If it does not, the runtime
simply JITs a different key (one cold compile) and the prebuilt entry is unused; exactness does not depend on the
tile config (EXACTNESS.md section 2).

To do in the window (CPU only, nice 19, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES empty, ~1-3 min per kernel):
  python3 install.py prejit        # per node, after install; refuses on any sha/key/compiler mismatch
  python3 install.py prejit-status
  then (optional, evidence) on spark-eight:  cuobjdump -sass <new>/kernel.cubin vs the 38370f02 cubin: expect the
  same instruction sequence (HMMA/QMMA count, loop structure) with only N-derived immediates different.
After the first boot with the flag on, record `install.py prejit-status` cubin sha256 into KIT.json prejit.*.cubin_sha256
so later installs can verify byte-identical builds across nodes.

Fix pass (2026-11-08 ~14:50Z): read-only key computation on spark-eight
------------------------------------------------------------------------
spark-one was unreachable (ssh: host down) at that time; spark-eight was reachable and had no CLUSTER_LOCK. Nothing was
compiled or written there: tools/djkey.py was piped over stdin into `nice -n 19 ~/venvs/vllm032/bin/python -I -`,
which only read ~/.cache/vllm/deep_gemm/cache and vllm/third_party/deep_gemm/include.
  src 2201c753 selfkey True  src kernel.cu 301a0d1e  -> new kernel.cu fc936b78  new key 5a63770a66faeaa4f1203886b22d547d (absent)
  src 5559d059 selfkey True  src kernel.cu d88102be  -> new kernel.cu 6a9ee0f9  new key 3a6d4662 == KIT.json   (absent)
  src 4ea90a59 selfkey True  (target 128x64 N768 E384) -> 8135464c == the LIVE target-compact entry (present)
  src 0e915d63 selfkey True  (target 128x128 N768 E384) -> ec8c0dc5 == the LIVE target-compact entry (present)
So both 128-row tile configs map N768 -> N576 one to one on the target, which supports the analogy for the drafter.
Cubins of identical kernel.cu differ between nodes (5559d059: 84ecdc26 on spark-one per the build pass, 5cc4cce7 on
spark-eight), so cubin shas are recorded per node and never used as an install gate.
